# Wi-Fi: the coprocessor is not running

How sure we are: <span class="tag tag-hyp">HYPOTHESIS</span>

## What we know

The Wi-Fi reset line was toggled and read back. Every probed register of the SDIO block reads zero and a written value is
never read back. The start-up sequence of the embedded coprocessor involved in this path was read in its firmware, and
that firmware uses the standard SDHCI register layout.

## What we guess

The coprocessor may own the real SDIO window, with the main processor only posting messages to it. Which physical clock
gate belongs to the SDIO block, and to the coprocessor, is not known: the device tree's gate numbers are not the physical ones.

## What would settle it

A read-only survey of all the clock gates and of the clock mask registers is built and not run. It would tell which
blocks are clocked before anything is started.

*This describes an experiment, not a procedure to follow: a step that writes to the phone's hardware is only run after a written description and an explicit decision.*

~~Gate 0x27 read 0xF, so the coprocessor's clock was already on.~~

Withdrawn: gate 0x27 is the NAND controller 1's, not the coprocessor's. The coprocessor's clock state is unknown. [The iBSS clock initialisation](../../research/2026-10-16-touch-n88-preconditions.md#the-ibss-clock-initialisation-static-2026-10-16)

Caveat: the device tree's gate numbers are not physical indexes, so that run may not have enabled the block's clock. [Hardware map: Wi-Fi and SDIO](../../en/03-hardware-map.md#wi-fi-and-sdio)
